report.interpretation: Cycle time is the median days from report date to close date for closed claims, grouped by report month, as the agreed cycle_time_days metric defines it. I looked at Southeast (FL, GA, NC), comparing claims reported from May 2026 with those reported in Jan–Apr 2026. I left out August and September 2026 because most of those claims are still open, which makes their cycle times look artificially short.
report.answer: The slowdown is real. The Southeast median rose from about 28 days (Jan–Apr 2026 reports) to 38 days (May–Jul 2026 reports), peaking at 40 days for July. Other regions stayed flat (Texas actually got faster). The data points to a staffing shortfall. Two of the six Southeast adjusters left (ADJ-016 on 2026-05-01 and ADJ-017 on 2026-05-15), and none of their claims were reported after they left. The remaining four adjusters took over the same volume, so claims per adjuster rose from about 16 per month to about 26. Every remaining adjuster slowed down, by roughly 5 to 10 days. The slowdown appears across all three states, auto and home, and preferred and non-preferred shops. It doesn't look like a mix change in causes (bodily injury and liability share is steady at about 10%), a state, or a repair-network issue. The workload link is a strong correlation, not proof of cause. The Aug and Sep figures are not reliable yet.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adjuster departures raised workload and slowed closing
hypotheses.evidence: Adjusters ADJ-016 and ADJ-017 left on 2026-05-01 and 2026-05-15. Claim volume was unchanged, so claims per remaining adjuster rose about 60%, and cycle time rose at the same time.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shift toward slow-settling bodily injury and liability claims
hypotheses.evidence: Their share was about 8-11% before and after. Within property claims, the median days to close still rose (auto 20 to 27, home 35 to 52).

hypotheses.hypothesis: One state, one adjuster or the repair network
hypotheses.evidence: FL, GA and NC all slowed down. All four remaining adjusters slowed down. Preferred and non-preferred shops both slowed down (20 to 27 and 15.5 to 25 days).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Data artifact from incomplete recent months
hypotheses.evidence: The May–Jul comparison excludes the open-claim-heavy Aug and Sep. Aug (28 days) and Sep (9 days) look faster only because slow claims haven't closed yet.

hypotheses.hypothesis: External event such as a weather surge
hypotheses.evidence: Southeast claim volume rose only slightly from May to Jul (101 to 108 claims). I did not check the weather_events table in detail. Volume jumped in Aug to 143, which is outside the comparison window.

data_quality_issues.issue: Aug and Sep 2026 claims are largely still open (Sep: 21 of 135 closed). The metric counts closed claims only.
data_quality_issues.impact: The recent Southeast median days to close (28 for Aug, 9 for Sep) are misleadingly low and can't be used to say the slowdown has ended.

proposed_actions.title: Review Southeast adjuster staffing
proposed_actions.reason: Two adjusters left in May 2026 and were not replaced. The remaining four carry about 26 claims each per month, up from about 16, and Aug–Sep volume is higher still (143 and 135 claims).

open_questions: Were the departed adjusters' open claims reassigned, and was backfill hiring planned?
